title: Towards an Enhanced Understanding of Bias in Pre-trained Neural Language Models: A Survey with Special Emphasis on Affective Bias

bias_targets.methodology: Surveying methods that measure unfair or imbalanced associations of affect (emotions/sentiment) with key terms representing protected groups using sentiment analysis, emotion detection differences, directional sentiment vectors, and lexical scoring.

Surveying measurement techniques such as Word Embedding Association Test (WEAT), sequence likelihood, pronoun ranking, log probability bias scores, co-occurrence statistics, and context association tests (CAT).
Surveying evaluations through normalized probability, categorical bias scores, performance disparities on African American Vernacular English (AAVE), and word embedding association tests.
Reviewing methods such as prompt completion, analogical reasoning, and story generation analysis (e.g., using GPT-3).
Reviewing evaluations utilizing lexicon-based analysis, multinomial log-linear regression, and paired t-tests on sentiment scores for age-related keywords.
Reviewing methodologies including indirect and direct bias metrics, calculating differences in mean sentiment scores, and linear regression.
Reviewing the identification of bias through the mean score of predictions and linear regression on sentiment and toxicity scores for sentences mentioning persons with disabilities.
Reviewing evaluations that use model querying to predict pronouns at masked positions, language modelling scores, and stereotype scores.

Surveying methodologies like the Contextualized Embedding Association Test (CEAT), emergent intersectional bias detection, and measuring differences/similarities in sentiment scores across combined demographic domains.
